title: ALMA survey of massive cluster progenitors from ATLASGAL. Limited fragmentation at the early evolutionary stage of massive clumps
question: How do infrared-quiet massive ATLASGAL clumps (d ≤ 4.5 kpc) fragment from 0.3 pc to 0.06 pc scales at an early evolutionary stage?

what.value: Sample selection, clump masses, distances, T_d=18 K for clumps

evidence.quote: Column 10 gives the distance from Csengeri et al. (2017).
κ 870µm = 0.0185g cm −2 from Ossenkopf & Henning (1994) accounting for a gas-to-dust ratio of 100

recipe.method: Calibrate in CASA, average line-free channels, CLEAN with robust 0.5, primary beam correct
2D Gaussian fitting with Gaussclumps, sources down to ~7σ
Optically thin dust: M = S d² κ⁻¹ B(Td)⁻¹
assumptions: Td = 25 K for cores (factor of two mass uncertainty); κ870 = 0.0185 g cm-2; gas-to-dust 100

recipe.method: Least-square power-law fit above 50 Msun completeness limit; Monte Carlo over Td

recipe.goal: Compare with Jeans mass, turbulence and magnetic support
recipe.method: Thermal Jeans mass, Turbulent Core model, magnetic critical mass (Bertoldi & McKee)

evidence.quote: A total number of 124 fragments down to a ∼7 σ rms noise level
This gives on average, N¯ fr =3 sources per clump
the normal temperature distribution gives α MC =1.01±0.11
the most massive core with ∼400 M ⊙ within a deconvolved FWHM size of 0.054pc
The extracted cores have a mean mass of ∼63 M ⊙
We recover between 16-47% of the flux

score_reason: Short letter; main steps and numbers given, but imaging and extraction parameters are sparse.
